set.typical_award_size: Full or partial property tax exemption under Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g), prorated to the share of units occupied by lower income households. The owner needs a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate (and a Supplemental Clearance Certificate for a nonprofit or eligible LLC managing general partner) and files with the Madera County Assessor: BOE-267 (first filing) or BOE-267-A (annual), plus BOE-267-L for nonprofit-owned lower income housing or BOE-267-L1 for a limited partnership with an eligible managing general partner.
set.affordability_requirement: Lower income households as defined in HSC 50079.5 (80% AMI). Units must be restricted by a regulatory agreement with a public agency, recorded deed restriction or other legal document; the property must have tax credits or government financing, or, for a nonprofit owner without them, 90% or more lower income occupants; and the tax savings must be used to maintain affordability or reduce rents. The exemption covers only the qualifying share of units.
set.cycle_notes: Annual claim due to the County Assessor by February 15 each year (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). Late claims: 90% of tax, penalty and interest may be cancelled if filed by January 1 of the next year, 85% after that.
set.next_deadline: File BOE-267 or BOE-267-A with the supplemental affidavit at the Madera County Assessor by February 15, 2027 for the 2027-28 roll (that date is Presidents' Day, so if the office is closed the filing moves to the next business day).

set.typical_award_size: No published lending program. The City's FY 2024-25 ACFR shows the Low and Moderate Income Housing special revenue fund (former RDA housing funds) with a fund balance of $3,458,285 at June 30, 2025, up from $2,486,663, after FY 2024-25 revenue of $1,179,511 in property taxes and $117,379 in investment income, $8,828 of expenditures and a $316,440 transfer out; about $1.4 million budgeted for low and moderate income housing went unspent. Remaining RDA-era developer notes receivable total $7,000. The latest SB 341 reports posted are FY 2014-15 and FY 2015-16.
set.affordability_requirement: HSC 34176.1: funds go to households at or below 80% AMI; over each five-year period at least 30% of development spending must be rental housing for extremely low income (30% AMI) households and no more than 20% may serve households at 60-80% AMI. Up to $500,000 a year may go to homeless prevention and rapid rehousing. An unencumbered balance above the greater of $1,000,000 or the prior four years of deposits is excess surplus that must be committed within three years or sent to HCD.
set.layering_notes: Recorded so the asset fund is not overlooked. The FY 2024-25 ACFR shows about $3.5 million in the fund and roughly $1.2 million a year of incoming property tax revenue, but the City has no NOFA or lending guidelines for it; ask the City how it plans to deploy the balance and whether successor-owned parcels remain. Any award would layer with City HOME and PLHA, and the 30% extremely low income targeting rule favors deeply affordable rental projects.

set.typical_award_size: Location-based reduction of development impact fees under the Impact Fee Reduction Incentive Program (Resolution 2022-060): Infill Area fees 25% below Expansion Area and City Center fees 50% below. The current Citywide Master Fee Schedule (FY 2023-24, Resolution 2023-021) sets multifamily impact fees per unit of about $18,553 Expansion Area, $13,915 Infill Area and $9,277 City Center (the Housing Element's 2022 figures were $17,569, $13,177 and $8,785). The Regional Transportation Mitigation fee is reduced for affordable units ($821 per affordable multifamily unit). Development impact fee deferral program (approved May 26, 2015): applicant pays a nonrefundable 20% of impact fees at building permit application and the remaining 80% before final inspection; the City charges $400 to prepare a DIF deferral agreement. Housing Element Program 7 commits to continued fee reductions and deferrals for affordable and special-needs projects and lists reduced water and wastewater connection fees as a flexible standard.
set.per_unit_cap: Equal to the reduction; City Center saves about $9,277 per multifamily unit versus Expansion Area under the FY 2023-24 schedule.
